thought.text: The installation is complete and fully verified — the authenticated API returns real data from the database through the full Caddy→nginx→Django→PostGIS stack. All 9 services are up and healthy.

reasoning_content:
The authenticated API returns actual data: `{"id":1,"project":"Default","description":null,"active":true}` — the backend is reading from PostgreSQL via the full Caddy→nginx→Django→PostGIS stack.

Everything verified:
1. ✅ All 9 containers Up (db + qgis-server + tileserver are healthy)
2. ✅ Frontend: SvelteKit login page renders (303 → /login → full HTML)
3. ✅ API: DRF root is 200, JWT login is 200, authenticated project listing returns real data
4. ✅ Admin: 302 to login (auth flow works)
5. ✅ QGIS Server: WMS responds (400 without MAP param / with auth = proper QGIS ServerException XML)
6. ✅ TileServer: healthy, tilejson 200
7. ✅ WebDAV: 401 unauthenticated, 207 multi-status when authenticated
8. ✅ Database: 108 migrations, 103 tables, postgis + pgrouting + dblink + pgcrypto extensions, superuser created, qgis_user with correct permissions (denied on permission tables)
9. ✅ Caddy: local HTTPS via internal CA works for all *.localhost domains

The installation is complete and verified. Now, let me organize the final report.

Summary of what was done:
1. Environment: /workspace, Docker 29.7.2 + Compose v5.5.0 already installed; 8 CPU / 7.6 GB RAM (guide assumes 16GB, but it worked without issues).
2. Following the guide (Docker Compose Development path — the only path runnable without an external domain; the production path requires a Let's Encrypt domain):
   - Created /workspace/deployment/.env from the documented Section 2.1 values (Section 2.1 of the Deployment README), generating secrets, adding QGIS_DB_USER/QGIS_DB_PASSWORD (used by init.sh), API_URL/PUBLIC_API_URL/PUBLIC_TILE_SERVER_URL (build args), QGIS_PG_SERVICE_NAME.
   - Added app.localhost, files.localhost, qgis.localhost, tiles.localhost to DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS (necessary because the dev Caddyfile's forward_auth subrequests preserve the original Host; the .env in the docs is incomplete in this respect).
3. `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --build` — ran into and fixed the following issues:
   - **db build failure (documentation/external issue)**: the pinned base `postgis/postgis:17-3.5` (Debian bullseye, EOL) references `http://apt.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt bullseye-pgdg`, but this has been removed upstream (404). Fix: in deployment/postgres/Dockerfile, changed the PGDG source to `http://apt-archive.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt/` (the official PGDG archive that still serves the signed bullseye-pgdg suite); built postgresql-17-pgrouting 3.8.0.
   - **db startup failure (repo bug)**: `REVOKE ALL ON model_permission/route_permission` in deployment/postgres/init.sh references Django tables that don't yet exist at init time (created by migration 0057) → the entrypoint aborts (exit 3). Fix: wrapped the REVOKEs in an `IF EXISTS` block.
   - **nginx crash loop (dev compose bug)**: it was mounting `nginx/nginx.conf` (the full main config including `worker_processes` and cache zones) as `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` → "worker_processes not allowed here". Fix: mount both `nginx.conf` at /etc/nginx/nginx.conf (provides the wms_cache/mvt_cache zones that default.conf requires) and `default.conf` at conf.d/default.conf.
   - **qgis-server immediate exit (dev compose bug)**: the `>` folded scalar broke the `<<EOF` heredoc (the terminating `EOF` gets merged into the same line as content) → the rest of the command was swallowed as the heredoc body. Fix: rewrote the command as an explicit list with a `printf`-based pg_service.conf (the pattern from the production compose).
   - **missing backend-wms (dev compose bug)**: `nginx/default.conf` references `upstream backend_wms` but the service doesn't exist in the dev compose → nginx fails to resolve. Added the backend-wms service (mirroring production).
   - **tileserver crash loop (documented user prerequisite)**: `tiles/germany.mbtiles` is user-generated via Planetiler (not included in the repo). Created a minimal valid empty MBTiles placeholder so the service can start; real basemap data requires running Planetiler per the docs.
4. After clearing the half-initialized postgres bind mount, restarted the stack; the backend ran migrations, created the superuser, and loaded fixtures.
5. One-shot REVOKE applied to qgis_user (to match init.sh's intent, since migrations created the tables after init).
6. Verified all endpoints.

Known limitations / notes:
- The Wireguard service is intentionally omitted in the dev compose (it only exists in the production compose; it's an optional feature for QGIS Desktop DB access).
- germany.mbtiles is an empty placeholder — no tiles will render until Planetiler data is generated.
- The sandbox doesn't resolve *.localhost via DNS; I verified using curl --resolve to 127.0.0.1 (on a normal host the documented URLs work; Caddy's internal CA needs to be trusted for browser use).
- Host has 7.6GB RAM vs the guide's recommended 16GB — all services are running without issues (no deploy.memory limits in the dev compose).

Additional actions (beyond the guide):
- Modified deployment/postgres/Dockerfile (PGDG archive source)
- Modified deployment/postgres/init.sh (conditional REVOKE)
- Modified deployment/docker-compose.dev.yml (nginx volumes, qgis-server command, backend-wms service)
- Created deployment/tiles/germany.mbtiles placeholder
- Extended DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS beyond the documented example
- One-shot REVOKE against qgis_user
- Cleared the half-initialized postgres/data bind mount

Verification: all the curl checks above + docker compose ps.

Failure mode / attribution: null (success).

Let me write the final report.

action.message:
Qonnectra installed successfully via Docker Compose (development stack with local HTTPS) in /workspace/deployment. All 9 services are up and verified: db (healthy), backend, backend-wms, frontend, nginx, qgis-server (healthy), tileserver (healthy), caddy, pg-error-parser. Verified end-to-end: frontend login page renders (app.localhost), DRF API returns 200 with JWT login working (api.localhost), Django admin redirects to login (admin.localhost), QGIS WMS responds correctly, tileserver serves tilejson, WebDAV returns 401 unauth / 207 PROPFIND auth (files.localhost), and an authenticated API call returned real project data from the migrated PostGIS database.

Several repository defects had to be fixed to complete the documented installation:
1. deployment/postgres/Dockerfile: base image postgis/postgis:17-3.5 (Debian bullseye, EOL) references the bullseye-pgdg apt repo, which apt.postgresql.org has removed (404). Pointed the source to the official PGDG archive (apt-archive.postgresql.org) which still serves the signed bullseye suite; pgrouting 3.8.0 installs and CREATE EXTENSION pgrouting works.
2. deployment/postgres/init.sh: REVOKE ALL ON model_permission/route_permission fails on fresh install (tables created later by Django migration 0057), aborting DB init (exit 3). Made the REVOKEs conditional on table existence.
3. deployment/docker-compose.dev.yml: (a) nginx service mounted the full main nginx.conf as a site conf → "worker_processes not allowed here"; now mounts nginx.conf as main config plus default.conf; (b) qgis-server command used a folded scalar that broke its <<EOF heredoc (EOF terminator merged into content line, rest of command swallowed); rewritten as explicit list with printf; (c) backend-wms service was missing although nginx/default.conf defines upstream backend_wms; added it mirroring the production compose.
4. tiles/germany.mbtiles is user-generated (Planetiler, per deployment/README.md, not in repo); created a minimal valid empty MBTiles placeholder so tileserver starts (real basemap data still requires Planetiler).
Also extended DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS in deployment/.env with app.localhost, files.localhost, qgis.localhost, tiles.localhost (required by the dev Caddyfile's forward_auth subrequests; the documented .env example omits them), and applied the intended one-off REVOKE on the permission tables for qgis_user.
